correctness.rationale: Necessity: any violating pair of unequal overlapping non-singleton classes gives a singleton valuation such that one order retains a point of their set difference and the other deletes it; the case of proper containment is covered symmetrically. Sufficiency: only non-singleton mixed classes can be deleted. Under the proposed criterion each such deleted class is a union of complete classes of the other equivalence relation. Therefore the second condition is evaluated on unchanged or removed whole classes and the two results both equal the original homogeneous-set intersection. This works for infinite W. The combinatorial map to three-color partial partitions is invertible. A distinct finite checker exhaustively tests every partition pair for n<=5 and independent counting recurrence.

originality.rationale: Direct examination of the 2013 public-announcement knowing-whether paper, the September 2026 S5 dynamic epistemic calculus, and the September 2026 non-contingency sequent calculus finds the defining semantics and proof-theoretic results but not the asserted universal two-update order-independence classification. value.rationale: The frame characterization exactly determines when two natural epistemically conditioned model updates are order-independent for all valuations, without size or finiteness restrictions. Failure is detected by one-true-world tests, with an optimal three-world countermodel; the finite classification admits a deterministic near-linear test and gives a meaningful modal interpretation of a known set-partition sequence. The objective is the behavior of dynamic observations, not the pre-existing integer sequence or an arbitrary finite slice.
